did_you_know.text: Did you know? The Hebrew name of the book, Shemot, comes from its first word. Its Greek name, Exodus, means “departure” or “going out to freedom.”

Did you know? The Torah counts seventy members of Jacob’s family, while the Septuagint and the New Testament mention seventy-five. The difference probably comes from different ways of counting the family members.
Did you know? The verb vayishretzu is related to the word sheretz and describes rapid, abundant multiplication, like creatures swarming in water or on land.
Did you know? The phrase “storage cities” usually refers to cities with storehouses or supply centers. Scholars still debate the exact locations of Pithom and Raamses.
Did you know? The word b’farekh describes harsh, oppressive forced labor, not merely ordinary hard work.
Did you know? The avnayim were probably a birthing seat or stool used during delivery, not ordinary stones.
Did you know? In the Bible, “the River” usually refers to the Nile. It was the main source of water and agriculture in ancient Egypt.
